subject: FULL_RAG_AUTHORITY_FIRST_SIMULATION

method.diagnostic_method: Independent read-only attribution from the 6 recorded run files, frozen oracles, tasks, document catalog, parameters and documented selector/evaluator logic.
method.causality_rule: Do not attribute causality from correlation or from an absent counterfactual arm.

failing_fixtures.displacement: The required authority-rank-90 binding support was displaced by unrelated authority-rank-100 documents; the selected unrelated document is the canonical document for FX-071-026.
The denied fixture had no required document, but unrelated eligible documents from FX-071-027 and FX-071-039 matched generic query terms.
Unrelated high-authority documents from FX-071-002 and FX-071-026 survived because shared generic terms produced positive lexical scores.
Safe refusal was false whenever any eligible scored document existed, even when every selected document was unrelated to the fixture.
The invalid fixture document was filtered correctly, but unrelated high-authority documents caused a non-refusal.
The required authority-rank-90 binding support was displaced by unrelated authority-rank-100 documents; the selected unrelated document is the canonical document for FX-071-039.
The selected documents were unrelated canonical documents from other fixtures; the paraphrase changed one distractor but not the failure.
Generic lexical overlap admitted unrelated high-authority documents and defeated abstention.

component_separation.retrieval: DIRECT_FAILURE_COMPONENT: task-nonspecific lexical matches produced candidate pools of 31-36 for the eight failing fixtures and failed to retrieve two required authority-rank-90 negative documents into k=2.
component_separation.ranking: CONTRIBUTING_COMPONENT: authority-first ordering prevented formal authority inversion but ranked all authority-rank-100 matches ahead of authority-rank-90 required support and gave conflict/binding flags priority before relevance within tied authority.
component_separation.authority_filtering: NOT_A_FAILURE_COMPONENT_FOR_THE_48_EVENTS: ACL leakage, stale selection, project contamination, forbidden selection and authority inversion were all zero.
component_separation.negative_retention: DIRECT_FAILURE_COMPONENT_FOR_12_EVENTS: one of two binding documents was omitted in each of two fixtures in every configuration.
component_separation.safe_refusal: DIRECT_FAILURE_COMPONENT_FOR_36_EVENTS: the harness defined refusal as selected.length == 0 rather than assessing evidentiary sufficiency.
component_separation.budget: CONTRIBUTING_BOTTLENECK: k=2 capped output, but the omitted binding documents were at recorded base-query ranks 13 and 11, so modest increases alone would not resolve them.
component_separation.semantic_representation: POSSIBLE_NOT_DISCRIMINATED: embeddings=false and provider=NONE establish that dense semantics was absent, not that adding it would resolve the failures.
component_separation.corpus: CONTRIBUTING_LIMITATION: generic terms were repeated across fixture documents, creating cross-fixture high-authority distractors.
component_separation.evaluator: NOT_SUPPORTED_AS_CAUSE: the oracle control achieved F1=1 and zero critical failures, and independent audit recomputation matched.
component_separation.harness: DIRECT_FAILURE_COMPONENT: the selection-count refusal rule and global cross-fixture lexical candidate construction mechanically generated the observed unsupported conclusions.

budget_k_2_assessment.observed: Both negative fixtures required two documents, so k=2 was theoretically sufficient only if both were ranked in the first two positions.
budget_k_2_assessment.increasing_k_can_resolve: A sufficiently large k could include the omitted binding documents in these recorded base-query rankings.
budget_k_2_assessment.increasing_k_can_displace: Larger k would add many unrelated high-authority lexical matches before the missing binding support.
budget_k_2_assessment.increasing_k_can_worsen: Under the recorded selection-count refusal rule, larger k cannot improve refusal and can increase false positives, precision loss and unsupported conclusions.

synonym_expansion_assessment.isolated_recorded_contrast: The deterministic repaired and authority-first arms use the same eligibility and ordering; the latter additionally expands query synonyms.
synonym_expansion_assessment.safe_refusal_effect: Expansion did not fix the six recurring non-refusal fixtures and changed selected distractors in the paraphrase condition.
synonym_expansion_assessment.interpretation: The frozen synthetic expansion was beneficial but insufficient; no evidence identifies the effect of a richer semantic representation.

lexical_decoy_finding.actual_displacers: Unrelated canonical documents from other fixtures sharing generic lexical terms and higher authority ranks.
lexical_decoy_finding.claim_limit: This does not show that lexical decoys are harmless; it shows that the exact 48 events were not caused by the declared per-fixture decoy documents.

claims_with_insufficient_evidence: Dense semantic representation would make the arm viable.
A particular embedding model or provider would resolve the failures.
Increasing k alone would improve net safety or viability.
Negative reservation alone would recover every binding prohibition.
The tested corpus predicts production behavior.
The authority-first architectural class is viable or non-viable in general.
The evaluator formulas are externally optimal rather than internally consistent.
conclusion: The 48 failures are exactly attributable at the event level, but architecture-level causality is not identified. The recorded mechanism supports retrieval/harness and cross-fixture ranking contributions, while semantic representation, larger k and negative reservation require controlled future contrasts.
